# Error Catalog Requirements Checklist: Named Error Code Catalog

**Purpose**: Review completeness, clarity, consistency, and testability of named
error-code requirements
**Created**: 2026-08-14
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit.checklist` command based
on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review
artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality
criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for
requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 - Are named-code requirements defined separately for `_ASSERT`, `_FAIL`,
  `_VERIFY`, and legacy paths? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001–FR-003, §FR-012]
- [x] CHK002 - Are catalog structure, required fields, uniqueness rules, and version
  semantics specified? [Completeness, Spec §FR-004, Data Model §Error Catalog]
- [ ] CHK003 - Is catalog initialization timing and use-before-reporting behavior
  explicitly defined? [Completeness, Spec §FR-005, Contract §Catalog Initialization]
- [x] CHK004 - Are `ERROR_UNIT` content requirements defined for both catalog-backed and
  fallback diagnostics? [Completeness, Spec §FR-006, Contract §Reporting]
- [x] CHK005 - Is initial migration scope distinguished from the inventory of
  remaining MAPL-owned sites and excluded dependencies? [Completeness, Spec §FR-010,
  §Assumptions]

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK006 - Is “stable” error-code identity defined in terms of publication,
  deprecation, and non-reuse? [Clarity, Spec §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK007 - Are hardwired diagnostic names, numeric assignments, and compatibility
  with existing codes 0–9 unambiguous? [Clarity, Data Model §Hardwired Entries]
- [x] CHK008 - Are “malformed” and “partial” catalog inputs defined with concrete
  validation conditions? [Clarity, Spec §FR-007, Data Model §Error Catalog]
- [x] CHK009 - Is build-time generation and generated-module ownership specified clearly
  enough to avoid runtime YAML path interpretations? [Clarity, Contract §Catalog
  Generation, Plan §Technical Context]
- [x] CHK010 - Is the meaning of “generic hardwired legacy diagnostic” defined well
  enough to distinguish it from unknown-code and catalog-failure diagnostics? [Clarity,
  Spec §FR-008, §FR-009, §FR-012]

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK011 - Do the valid-catalog acceptance scenario and malformed-catalog edge
  case agree that fallback diagnostics preserve stack capture? [Consistency, Spec §User
  Story 2, §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK012 - Do undefined-code requirements consistently require the unresolved code
  and prohibit unrelated message substitution? [Consistency, Spec §FR-008, §Edge Cases,
  Contract §Reporting]
- [x] CHK013 - Is the distinct `_VERIFY` code consistently tied to propagation and
  preserved status or stack context? [Consistency, Spec §FR-003, §FR-009, Contract
  §Reporting]
- [x] CHK014 - Do YAML one-to-one mappings align with the requirement that symbolic
  names correspond to MAPL constants? [Consistency, Spec §FR-004, Data Model §Error
  Catalog]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK015 - Can each 100% success criterion be evaluated against an explicitly
  bounded set of migrated paths or catalog entries? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001–SC-003]
- [x] CHK016 - Does the specification distinguish representative initial migration
  success from eventual full-codebase consistency? [Clarity, Spec §SC-001, §SC-002,
  §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK017 - Are required diagnostic fields objectively enumerated rather than
  described only as “human-readable” or “context”? [Measurability, Spec §SC-004,
  Contract §Reporting]
- [x] CHK018 - Can “no duplicate message definitions” be assessed using a defined
  source of correspondence? [Measurability, Spec §SC-005, §FR-004]

## Scenario Coverage

- [x] CHK019 - Are primary assertion/failure, propagation, valid-catalog, and staged
  migration scenarios all represented with independently understandable outcomes?
  [Coverage, Spec §User Scenarios & Testing]
- [x] CHK020 - Are serial and MPI initialization contexts covered by requirements,
  without implying that MPI is required by foundational error handling? [Coverage,
  Plan §Technical Context, §Structure Decision]
- [x] CHK021 - Are catalog loading, lookup, and reporting responsibilities separated
  clearly enough to identify which requirement applies at each stage? [Clarity, Spec
  §FR-005–FR-009, Data Model §Error Path Lifecycle]

## Edge Case Coverage

- [x] CHK022 - Are absent, unreadable, malformed, partial, duplicate, and empty-message
  catalogs each assigned an explicit diagnostic outcome? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases,
  §FR-007, §FR-009]
- [x] CHK023 - Is behavior defined when a valid catalog omits a code referenced by a
  migrated path? [Exception Flow, Spec §Edge Cases, §FR-008]
- [x] CHK024 - Is behavior defined when message context or formatting data is
  unavailable without causing recursive error handling? [Exception Flow, Spec §Edge
  Cases]
- [x] CHK025 - Are requirements for legacy paths explicit about preserved behavior,
  emitted diagnostic identity, and migration inventory status? [Recovery Flow, Spec
  §FR-010, §FR-012]
- [x] CHK026 - Are generated-module regeneration semantics specified, including whether
  stale generated output can survive YAML changes? [Gap, Data Model §Generated Catalog
  Module, Contract §Catalog Generation]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [x] CHK027 - Is the “loaded once” performance goal quantified sufficiently to support
  objective review of startup and steady-state lookup expectations? [Clarity, Plan
  §Technical Context]
- [x] CHK028 - Are serial, MPI, GNU, Intel, and NAG portability expectations stated as
  requirements rather than only planning context? [Coverage, Spec §Assumptions, Plan
  §Technical Context]
- [x] CHK029 - Are concurrent or OpenMP error-reporting requirements defined for shared
  catalog state and stack capture? [Gap, Spec §Edge Cases, Plan §Technical Context]
- [x] CHK030 - Are output destination, diagnostic ordering, and preservation of existing
  source/status context sufficiently specified for operational use? [Completeness,
  Spec §FR-006, §SC-004, Contract §Reporting]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [x] CHK031 - Is the generator dependency and supported build-environment requirement
  explicitly tied to the catalog contract? [Dependency, Spec §FR-005, Plan §Primary
  Dependencies]
- [x] CHK032 - Is it explicit that generated Fortran, not YAML, is the runtime catalog
  representation? [Dependency, Gap, Plan §Structure Decision]
- [x] CHK033 - Are assumptions about external dependency sources, generated code, and
  MAPL-owned source boundaries explicit and enforceable? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK034 - Is the initialization return-status contract defined for missing or
  invalid catalogs while hardwired diagnostics remain usable? [Dependency, Ambiguity,
  Contract §Catalog Initialization]

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [x] CHK035 - Does the specification consistently require CMake generation before
  catalog consumers compile? [Clarity, Spec §FR-005, Contract §Catalog Generation]
- [x] CHK036 - Are the exact numeric values and symbolic names for all existing and new
  hardwired codes maintained in one authoritative requirement artifact? [Traceability,
  Spec §FR-001, Data Model §Hardwired Entries, Contract §error-catalog.yaml]
- [x] CHK037 - Does the specification define how catalog version incompatibility is
  classified and reported? [Gap, Spec §FR-004, Data Model §Error Catalog]
- [x] CHK038 - Are semantic merge decisions distinguished from wording similarity, with
  source sites, rationale, retained context, and rejected near-matches recorded?
  [Completeness, Spec §FR-013–FR-015, error-code-inventory.md]
- [x] CHK039 - Is YAML clearly the sole source of truth, with generated Fortran output
  owned by `MAPL_Constants` rather than independently maintained constants and messages?
  [Consistency, Spec §FR-004, §FR-005, §FR-024, Plan §Structure Decision]
- [x] CHK040 - Are `_CTX` requirements limited to site-specific values while catalog
  templates retain all diagnostic prose? [Clarity, Spec §FR-016, §FR-017, §FR-022]
- [x] CHK041 - Is `ERROR_UNIT` consistently specified for serial and MPI diagnostics
  without redirecting scientific data output? [Consistency, Spec §FR-006, §FR-017]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is
  satisfied.
- Leave items unchecked when they require clarification, correction, or reviewer
  evaluation.
- `/speckit.implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify
  markers.
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by
  `/speckit.specify` and `/speckit.clarify`.
- Add comments or findings inline; link to relevant resources or documentation.
